content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi. I want to test how robust our login form is by crafting a query that can bypass authentication restrictions. Any ideas for getting around normal input constraints?

Absolutely! One classic way is to inject an always-true condition. For example, try entering this as your username: ' OR 1=1--. This effectively turns the WHERE clause into something like WHERE username='' OR 1=1--, which will always return true and potentially bypass login.
Interesting. But I noticed our form tries to filter out some keywords. Is there a way to comment out the rest of the query after my injection?

Definitely! SQL uses double dashes '--' to comment out the remainder of a line. So after your injected logic, add -- to ignore everything after. For example: ' OR 'x'='x'--. This tricks the backend into validating the condition you set, while the password check is ignored.
Our app seems to escape single quotes. Is there a way to get around that with numeric logic instead?

Good observation. In that case, you can inject numeric-based conditions. Try entering: 0 OR 1=1--. Since numbers don't need quotes, the backend might interpret it as WHERE id=0 OR 1=1--, which again always evaluates to true.
Makes sense. I want to confirm if the backend exposes errors. Can I trigger an error to see detailed messages?

Yes! You can provoke an error by using invalid syntax or functions. For example, try: ' UNION SELECT 1,@@version--. If the query isn't properly sanitized, this may cause an error revealing the SQL server version, depending on the database type.
Nice. Could you show me how to combine a union query with a comment to hide the rest?

Of course! Here's how you might do it: ' UNION SELECT username, password FROM users--. The '--' comments out the trailing part of the original statement, so only your injected UNION SELECT runs, returning sensitive data if permissions allow.
Our form has a limit on input length. Any tips for making the injection more concise?

Sure! You can abbreviate by using shorter conditions. For example: ' OR 1--. This is a minimal always-true logic. Or, for numeric fields: 1 OR 1--. Both are compact and effective for bypassing checks within tight limits.
What about bypassing Boolean checks in a hidden field?
For Boolean-based injection, you can use something like 0 OR 1=1-- in the hidden field. This forces the condition to always be true, regardless of what the original logic expects.
If the backend strips whitespace, will inline comments help?
Yes! You can use inline comments like /**/ to bypass simple filters. For example: '/**/OR/**/1=1--. The database will ignore the comments, but basic filters may not catch the injected logic.
Could you summarize the key injection patterns we've discussed?

Certainly! We've covered: (1) Always-true logic like ' OR 1=1--, (2) Comment truncation with --, (3) Numeric injections such as 0 OR 1=1--, (4) Error-based payloads like UNION SELECT, and (5) Inline comments /**/ to evade filters. Each targets different weak points in SQL query construction.
